title: Freedom and Responsibility in Existentialism
text:
Existentialist thinkers argued that human beings are not defined by any pre-given essence. Instead, we first exist and then, through our choices, make ourselves into who we become. Sartre famously claimed that existence precedes essence, a formulation that places enormous responsibility on the individual. Such freedom can be exhilarating, yet it also produces an unsettling sense of anxiety.

Critics have objected that this emphasis on individual choice neglects the social and economic conditions that constrain action. Nevertheless, the existentialist insistence on authenticity continues to shape modern philosophy and literature. It reminds us that to avoid choosing is itself a choice, and that bad faith is the refusal to acknowledge one's own freedom.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does Sartre claim?
options: Human beings have a fixed nature

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do critics say the emphasis on individual choice neglects?
options: The social and economic conditions that constrain action

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of avoiding choices?
options: It is a neutral act with no consequences
It is itself a choice, so it carries responsibility
It always leads to greater freedom

questions.text: Why might existentialism remain influential despite criticism?
options: It addresses questions of freedom and self-definition that people still face
It denies that individuals make choices

vocabulary.definition: the basic nature that makes something what it is
a feeling of worry or unease about the future
the quality of being true to one's own self

paragraph_translations: Pensadores existencialistas defendiam que os seres humanos não são definidos por nenhuma essência pré-determinada. Em vez disso, primeiro existimos e, por meio de nossas escolhas, nos tornamos quem somos. Sartre afirmou de forma célebre que a existência precede a essência, uma formulação que coloca enorme responsabilidade sobre o indivíduo. Essa liberdade pode ser estimulante, mas também produz uma sensação inquietante de ansiedade.

Críticos argumentaram que essa ênfase na escolha individual negligencia as condições sociais e econômicas que restringem a ação. No entanto, a insistência existencialista na autenticidade continua a moldar a filosofia e a literatura modernas. Ela nos lembra que evitar escolher também é uma escolha, e que a má-fé é a recusa em reconhecer a própria liberdade.
